name: Via Stitching
description: Stitch copper zones together with a grid of vias on a chosen net
description_full:
Fills the overlap of a net's copper zones (for example the top and bottom GND pours) with a grid of stitching vias, on whichever two copper layers you pick.

Built on KiCad's modern IPC API (kicad-python / kipy), so it keeps working on KiCad 11 and later, where the legacy SWIG pcbnew bindings are removed.

Features:
- Through, Micro, Blind, Buried, and Blind/Buried via types. Start/End Layer is free for every type except Through (always F.Cu/B.Cu); a non-standard combination for the chosen type prompts you to confirm rather than blocking it outright.
- Select an existing via first to pre-fill the dialog with its type, layers, net, diameter, and drill.
- Hexagonal, square, or staggered via patterns with configurable diameter, drill, and spacing.
- X/Y offset, for stitching more than one via pattern onto the same net and area (for example a separate front-side and back-side microvia pass) without them landing on top of each other.
- Vias are placed only where the net is poured on the layers the via connects, inset enough to stay clear of other-net copper on those layers.
- Tracks, pad copper, filled zones, and rule areas of other nets are avoided on the layers the via actually spans (every copper layer for a through via, just the relevant ones for a microvia or blind/buried via).
- Existing via and pad drill holes are avoided with a hole-to-hole margin, scoped to vias whose layer span overlaps the new one's. Milled slots get a keepout following their long axis rather than a circle as wide as the slot is long.
- Clearances come from the board's netclasses.
- A grid position blocked by a pad or a track is moved to the nearest clear spot instead of being dropped, so the grid keeps its coverage beside pads. The move is bounded by a quarter of the spacing and by the hole-to-hole margin, so the result still reads as a grid.
- Optional keepouts for other nets' filled zones, for footprint bodies, and for pads already on the stitched net (off by default, so via arrays under a QFN or BGA ground pad are not blocked).
- All placed vias are bundled into a single named group so they can be deleted as a set.
